html:
The Ngarrindjeri are the Aboriginal Australian people of the lower Murray River, the lakes at its mouth, the eastern Fleurieu Peninsula and the Coorong in South Australia. The name means "belonging to men" and covers a group of related clans.

The lakes and the Coorong gave fish, waterbirds and shellfish in plenty, and the Ngarrindjeri lived in large, settled communities. Their law and land are bound up with the Dreaming story of Ngurunderi, who made the river.

Smallpox came down the Murray before the settlers did. After South Australia was founded in 1836, their lands were taken quickly. In 1859 a mission opened at Raukkan (Point McLeay). The writer and inventor David Unaipon, born there in 1872, is on Australia's fifty dollar note. In the 1990s Ngarrindjeri women opposed a bridge to Hindmarsh Island, a dispute that went to a royal commission.

Their neighbours included the Peramangk and the Bindjali.
